//: The Ecom (Synergy ERP) QA-format sheet: Synergy_ERP_Test_Cases_Sheet_Format.xlsx, tab 'Test Cases'. 16 columns, read on 2026-11-07 from the workbook's own header row — not transcribed from the brief. Neither that workbook nor the automation one is in this repo and neither may be.
//method: The header row was read by an INDEPENDENT OOXML parser and by this repo's readSheetGrid, then compared cell by cell: 15,808 cells, zero mismatches (§AK). That comparison is also what found the attribute-order bug that had made the workbook unreadable — before it, readSheetGrid refused this file outright with 'workbook declares no sheets'.
//noPreconditions: There is NO Preconditions column and NO Type column, and both are therefore ABSENT rather than declared-and-blank. readFinalTestCases reports them in `absentColumns`, which is the difference between 'a QA could fill this in' and 'there is nowhere to fill it in'. The precondition is instead embedded in the Given cell as '(Precondition: ...)' — measured: 953 of 987 rows. NOTHING SPLITS IT OUT YET; that is a transformation, not a layout, and it is deferred rather than silently half-done.
//measured: 987 non-blank data rows; 987 distinct (Scenario ID, Test Case ID) pairs; 0 rows missing either id; 0 repeated pairs. Also measured, because it decides what a run can do with a row: `And` is EMPTY in 788 of 987 rows, and 734 Then cells hold several '- ' bullet lines — every one that has a bullet has more than one. A Then cell carrying four bullets is four assertions in one cell, and the reader makes it ONE clause.
//generated: The sheet was AI-generated from requirement documents and walkthrough videos, which is recorded here because it bears on trust: these clauses have not been through a human run, so a Status column is empty by construction rather than by neglect.
//clauseSeparator: Measured on this sheet: `&` appears in 0 of 987 `And` cells, so nothing is split by it today. Declared anyway rather than left to the default, so the value this sheet is read with is written down where it was measured.
